stage: HISTORIE (engine stage 6) - fractal axis + competing frames - cache
disputedNote: Even where this story begins is disputed - picking a start date is itself a position. Frames change emphasis and annotation, never the record.

frames.label: Jun 10, 2026 Balashikha blast
frames.note: This is the frame Russian state outlets and the Kremlin open with. The story begins as a criminal car bombing on Russian soil that killed Damir Davydov, with the FSB opening a murder probe. Read this way, the situation is a domestic terror incident in a Moscow suburb.

frames.label: Dec 2024 Kirillov killing
frames.note: This is the frame many Western and Ukrainian outlets open with, citing the IBT and Le Monde framing of a one-year pattern. The story begins with the December 2024 car bomb that killed Lt. Gen. Igor Kirillov and reads as the latest entry in a serial campaign of targeted strikes on senior Russian military figures. Read this way, June 2026 is a continuation, not a start.

frames.label: Feb 2022 full-scale invasion
frames.note: This is the frame Kyiv, the E3 envoys in Moscow, and most Ukrainian-aligned analysts open with. The story begins when Russia's full-scale invasion turned military logistics chiefs like Davydov into wartime actors, with assassinations read as battlefield-adjacent operations. Read this way, the Balashikha bomb is one node in a war that started four years earlier.

bands.label: Balashikha bombing and aftermath
bands.summary: Damir Davydov is killed by a car bomb in a Moscow suburb on June 10, drone strikes hit the capital region, and the E3 ambassadors meet Russia's deputy foreign minister as Britain seizes a Russian tanker.

nodes.title: Car bomb kills Russian military official Damir Davydov in Balashikha
nodes.what: A car bomb detonated in the Moscow suburb of Balashikha on June 10, killing Damir Davydov, identified in reporting as a senior figure tied to Russia's military ammunition supply. Russian authorities opened a murder probe and Reuters noted Russian investigators were looking at two car bombs in the Moscow area the same day. Video of the destroyed vehicle circulated through international outlets within hours.
nodes.disputed: TASS and other Russian state outlets describe the blast as a domestic criminal terror incident under FSB investigation; the New York Times, Reuters and International Business Times UK describe it as the latest in a sequence of targeted strikes on senior Russian military figures inside Russia.

nodes.title: UK, French and German envoys meet Russian deputy foreign minister
nodes.what: The ambassadors of Britain, France and Germany arrived at the Russian foreign ministry on June 11 for a roughly 90-minute meeting with Deputy Foreign Minister Alexander Galuzin. The encounter, described in Russian and Ukrainian coverage as a rare high-level contact in Moscow, took place a day after the Balashikha car bomb and amid an E3 push on Ukraine.

nodes.title: Moscow mayor reports drones shot down on approach to the capital
nodes.what: Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said on June 12 that 13 drones had been shot down on approach to the city, a count he later raised to 21 over the course of the day. The strikes came as Russian investigators were still working the Balashikha case and as the E3 ambassadors held their Moscow meeting.

nodes.title: Russia and Belarus announce joint counter-sanctions initiatives
nodes.what: The Russian foreign ministry said on June 13 that Moscow and Minsk had adopted a joint package of initiatives aimed at countering Western sanctions. The announcement was published the same week as the Balashikha bombing and the E3 ambassadors' visit, and was framed by TASS as part of Russia's response to pressure from European capitals.

nodes.title: Britain seizes Russian oil tanker as drones again target Moscow region
nodes.what: British authorities seized a Russian-linked oil tanker in the English Channel on June 14, an action Press TV connected to rising tensions with Moscow. The same day, TASS reported that Russian air defenses destroyed four UAVs heading toward the capital, extending the run of drone incidents around Moscow that began earlier in the week.

bands.label: Serial strikes on senior officers
bands.summary: A pattern of high-profile assassinations inside Russia opens with the December 2024 killing of Lt. Gen. Igor Kirillov and continues through further attacks on military and defense-linked figures.

nodes.title: Lt. Gen. Igor Kirillov killed by bomb in Moscow
nodes.what: Igor Kirillov, head of Russia's Nuclear, Biological and Chemical Protection Troops, and his assistant were killed when an explosive device hidden in an electric scooter detonated outside an apartment block on Ryazansky Prospekt in Moscow. Ukraine's SBU security service publicly claimed responsibility the same day, describing Kirillov as a legitimate target. Russia's Investigative Committee opened a terrorism case.

nodes.title: Lt. Gen. Yaroslav Moskalik killed by car bomb in Balashikha
nodes.what: Yaroslav Moskalik, deputy head of the main operations directorate of the Russian General Staff, was killed when a Volkswagen Golf packed with explosives detonated as he passed it in the Moscow region town of Balashikha. Russia's Investigative Committee opened a terrorism inquiry and later named a suspect it said had been recruited by Ukrainian intelligence; Kyiv did not officially claim the strike.

bands.label: Full-scale war years
bands.summary: Russia's February 2022 invasion of Ukraine reshaped the security picture, drew sanctions, and turned Russian ammunition and logistics commands into named wartime roles.

nodes.title: Russia launches full-scale invasion of Ukraine
nodes.what: Russian forces crossed Ukrainian borders from the north, east, and south in the early hours of February 24, opening a wider war that followed eight years of conflict in the Donbas. Western capitals imposed sweeping sanctions within days, and Ukraine declared martial law and general mobilization.

nodes.title: Daria Dugina killed by car bomb near Moscow
nodes.what: Dugina, daughter of Russian nationalist commentator Alexander Dugin, was killed when an explosive device detonated in the SUV she was driving on the outskirts of Moscow. The FSB blamed Ukrainian intelligence within days of the blast.
nodes.disputed: Russian state investigators described the killing as a Ukrainian-organized operation; Ukrainian officials described it as a Russian internal incident with no Ukrainian role.

nodes.title: Putin orders partial mobilization
nodes.what: President Vladimir Putin announced a partial military mobilization, calling up reservists to reinforce the front in Ukraine. The order was followed within days by referendums in occupied Ukrainian regions and a formal annexation declaration covering Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia, and Kherson.

nodes.title: ICC issues arrest warrant for Putin
nodes.what: The International Criminal Court issued arrest warrants for Vladimir Putin and Russian children's rights commissioner Maria Lvova-Belova, citing the unlawful deportation of children from occupied Ukrainian territory to Russia. Moscow rejected the court's jurisdiction.

nodes.title: Bombing kills milblogger Vladlen Tatarsky in St Petersburg
nodes.what: Pro-war military blogger Maxim Fomin, known as Vladlen Tatarsky, was killed when an explosive device concealed in a statuette detonated at a St Petersburg cafe event. Russian authorities detained a Russian woman, Darya Trepova, and described the attack as Ukrainian-directed.

nodes.title: Wagner chief Prigozhin killed in plane crash
nodes.what: Yevgeny Prigozhin, head of the Wagner private military company, died with senior Wagner leadership when their business jet crashed in Tver region north of Moscow. The crash came two months after Prigozhin's short-lived armed mutiny against the Russian Ministry of Defense.
nodes.disputed: Western governments and many analysts described the crash as a Kremlin-directed killing; Russian officials described it as an aviation incident under investigation.

bands.label: Crimea and Donbas decade
bands.summary: Russia's 2014 annexation of Crimea and the war in eastern Ukraine set the long arc of confrontation with NATO capitals, sanctions regimes, and the diplomatic break that the 2026 Moscow meetings still reference.

nodes.title: Russia signs treaty incorporating Crimea
nodes.what: Two days after a referendum organized under Russian military presence, Vladimir Putin signed a treaty in the Kremlin formally absorbing Crimea and Sevastopol into the Russian Federation. The United States and European Union imposed a first wave of sanctions on Russian and Crimean officials.
nodes.disputed: Russian officials presented the move as restoring a historic Russian territory after a legitimate vote; Ukraine, the EU, and most UN General Assembly members described it as an illegal annexation and the referendum as invalid.

nodes.title: Armed conflict opens in the Donbas
nodes.what: Pro-Russian groups seized administrative buildings in Donetsk and Luhansk and proclaimed separatist republics, prompting Kyiv to launch what it called an Anti-Terrorist Operation. Fighting quickly drew in heavy weapons and produced the first sustained casualties of the Donbas war.
nodes.disputed: Ukrainian and Western accounts describe the takeovers as directed and reinforced from Russia; Russian officials described the fighters as local volunteers responding to events in Kyiv.

nodes.title: Malaysia Airlines Flight 17 is shot down over Donetsk region
nodes.what: A Malaysia Airlines Boeing 777 flying from Amsterdam to Kuala Lumpur was destroyed in flight over separatist-held territory in eastern Ukraine, killing all 298 people on board. The Dutch-led Joint Investigation Team concluded the aircraft was struck by a Buk surface-to-air missile.
nodes.disputed: The Joint Investigation Team and a Dutch court tied the missile launcher to a Russian military unit and convicted several defendants in absentia; Russia rejected the findings and offered alternative explanations involving Ukrainian forces.

nodes.title: Minsk II package of measures signed
nodes.what: Leaders of Germany, France, Russia, and Ukraine met in Minsk and endorsed a thirteen-point package brokered with the OSCE, calling for a ceasefire, heavy weapons withdrawal, prisoner exchanges, and a political settlement for Donbas. The UN Security Council endorsed the package in Resolution 2202.
nodes.disputed: Kyiv described the agreement as a Russian-imposed framework signed under battlefield pressure that it could not fully implement; Moscow described Ukraine as the side that refused to carry out the political clauses.

nodes.title: Russian forces seize Ukrainian vessels in the Kerch Strait
nodes.what: Russian coast guard ships rammed and fired on three Ukrainian navy boats near the Kerch Strait, capturing 24 sailors and the vessels themselves. The incident triggered martial law in parts of Ukraine and a new round of Western diplomatic protests.

nodes.title: Russia massed forces near Ukraine and issued security demands
nodes.what: Western intelligence agencies and commercial satellite imagery tracked a major buildup of Russian troops, armor, and supplies along Ukraine's borders and in Belarus. Moscow circulated draft treaties to NATO and Washington demanding the alliance halt eastward enlargement and pull back forces from member states.
nodes.disputed: NATO capitals described the buildup as preparation for a possible large-scale invasion and the draft treaties as non-starters; Russian officials described the deployments as routine exercises and the proposals as legitimate security guarantees.
